title: Prober-initiated graduated cutoff for regional + tier routing
creator: Ana Patel
description:
Background: We currently rely primarily on passive telemetry (429 spikes, increased p50/p95 latency, error-rate deltas) to trigger model fallback and regional cutovers. That approach catches problems but is slow to detect regressions in degraded variants or cross-tenant noisy neighbors. We need a low-risk mechanism that accelerates safe fallbacks without inducing cascading failovers.

Proposal summary: Implement a prober-driven graduated cutoff and circuit that augments passive signals with targeted active probes and a multi-stage soft-cutoff. Prober-based decisions allow short, scoped checks against a candidate fallback model/region variant prior to broad rerouting. The system will: 1) run lightweight probes (synthetic requests with pinned prompts) to candidate fallback endpoints when passive signals cross preliminary thresholds (e.g., sustained 429 > 1.5x baseline for 30s or timeout rate > 1% in 60s), 2) decide using a combined score (probe success, realtime error-rate, latency delta) whether to apply a staged soft-cutoff (traffic fraction shift) or fully open a circuit breaker for a tenant/route/region.

Key behaviors and differentiators: 
- Probe-first: Only escalate to active probes when passive heuristics indicate unusual behavior. Probes are short (<= 500 tokens, 1–3 representative prompts) and use isolated, low-cost model variants to avoid impacting production quotas.
- Graduated cutoffs: Instead of immediate all-or-nothing failover, apply staged reductions (e.g., 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with hold windows and metrics re-evaluation between steps. Each step requires probe pass criteria or expiration of cooldown.
- Tenant-aware hysteresis: Circuits are tracked per-tenant and per-route (not global) with exponential backoff cooldowns and decay windows. We store a concise trip score (string token) with decay to avoid flip-flopping during noisy bursts.
- Multi-signal scoring: Final decision uses a weighted score composed of probe success rate, 1m error-rate delta, 95th latency delta, and recent 429 spike magnitude. Weights are tunable via config and default to conservative values favoring probe evidence.
- Probe isolation and safety: Probes run through a dedicated prober pool with separate quotas and observability. Probes never trigger billing events and have a fast timeout to avoid adding load.
- Soft fallback verification: Before sending the last 50% of traffic to a fallback model variant, the rollout controller validates that fallback returns coherent structured outputs for a small set of golden prompts and that embedding distances remain within expected ranges (for reranking/embeddings flows).

Threshold recommendations (starting defaults): 
- Passive trigger thresholds: 429 spike > 1.5x baseline sustained for 30s OR timeout rate > 0.5% over 60s OR error-rate (5xx) > 0.75% over 60s => schedule probes.
- Probe pass criteria: >= 80% probe success (no 429/timeout/5xx) AND median latency <= 1.5x baseline for that variant.
- Stage cutoffs: step1 = 10% traffic shift, hold 30s; step2 = 50% shift, hold 60s; step3 = 100% shift (full fallback). Each step requires either probe pass or passive signal trending downward.
- Circuit open: If after stage3 the error-rate remains > baseline+1% for 2m, open circuit for tenant-route and set cooldown 5m * attempts (exponential).

Data/telemetry needed: Prober success/failure metrics, per-probe latency histograms, per-tenant rolling error rates, 429/timeouts histograms, stage transitions, and rollout audit events. Add tracing spans linking probe runs to the originating passive signal.

Rollout plan: 
1) Implement prober service and API (worker + controller) behind feature flag.
2) Add passive trigger hooks in router to schedule probes.
3) Add graduated cutoff controller to rollout service with staged traffic shifting primitives.
4) QA: synthetic chaos tests (inject 429s/timeouts in staging), tenant-isolation tests, and scale tests to validate prober pool sizing.
5) Phased rollout: internal tenants -> small external tenants (opt-in) -> global enabled-by-default.

Open questions / trade-offs: 
- Probe prompt selection: randomization vs curated golden prompts. Curated prompts improve signal but risk overfitting to narrow correctness. Suggest hybrid: 2 golden + 1 random per probe.
- Cost vs safety: Probers increase CPU/GPU cycles. We will rate-limit probes and reuse low-cost model variants where possible.
- Storage: Trip scoring state per tenant introduces a small datastore footprint; propose an LRU in-memory store backed by Redis with TTL.

Success metrics: Reduce false-positive full cutovers by 45% and reduce mean time to safe fallback by 35% in chaos runs. Keep probe-induced additional token cost <0.3% of total tokens.

Docs & artifacts: Design doc in Confluence: https://company.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RI/pages/Prober+Fallback+Design, prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prober/pull/72, staging dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ab12/prober-fallback-staging
comments: 2026-03-02 - Ana Patel: Drafted proposal and shared with routing/serving leads. Initial thumbs-up from Maya (serving).
2026-03-04 - Mark Liu: Implemented prober worker scaffold. Initial unit tests for probe scheduling are green. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prober/pull/72
2026-03-06 - Priya Nair (DevOps): Suggested using a separate Redis namespace for trip-state to avoid key collisions with throttling. Will follow up on capacity sizing.
2026-03-08 - Security review note: probes must not exfiltrate tenant prompts; ensure probe inputs are sanitized or generated from golden set. Security review flagged for later sign-off.

2026-03-10 - Mark Liu: Added staged rollout controller and smoke tests; observed prober-induced 0.12% increase in token usage in staging. Next: add tenant hysteresis decay test and canary enablement UI in Console.
